newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices seen rising 0.25 point.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices seen rising 0.25 point.

text.p: Danish bond prices moved up in early trade on Wednesday and dealers expected benchmark gains of around 0.25 point during the day, on the back of German rises.
"The market is quite positive and we expect new high prices, but an unaltered spread of 60 (basis points to the 10-year bund), a dealer said.
At 0640 GMT the seven percent 2007 government bond, due to become the benchmark on September 1, was up 0.09 point from Tuesday's close, to 105.35 yielding 6.27 percent.
Its spread to the bund closed one basis point to 60 bp.
The crown firmed slightly to 3.8065 to the mark from 3.8067.
